'''Binignit''' is a [[Visayas|Visayan]] [[Soup#Dessert|dessert soup]] from the central [[Philippines]]. The dish is traditionally made with [[glutinous rice]] cooked in [[coconut milk]] with various slices of [[Saba banana|sabá bananas]], [[taro]], [[purple yam|ube]], and [[sweet potato]], among other ingredients.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://www.pinoyrecipe.net/binignit-recipe/ | title = Cebu Binignit Recipe |website = Pinoy Recipe At Iba Pa |access-date = February 25, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.ex-designz.net/recipedisplay.asp?rid=1522| title = Filipino Recipe |author=Maya |website=Ex-Designz Online Resources |date=2006-01-08 |access-date = April 3, 2010 |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110723123946/http://www.ex-designz.net/recipedisplay.asp?rid=1522| archive-date = July 23, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.everythingcebu.com/bits-and-pieces/binignit-and-biko/| title = Binignit and Biko| work = Everything Cebu| access-date = April 3, 2010| archive-date = June 19, 2010| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100619095351/http://www.everythingcebu.com/bits-and-pieces/binignit-and-biko/| url-status = dead}}</ref>  It is comparable to various dessert ''[[ginataan|guinataán]]'' (coconut milk-based) dishes found in other regions, such as ''[[bilo-bilo]]''. Among the [[Visayan people]], the dish is traditionally served on [[Good Friday]] of [[Holy Week in the Philippines|Holy Week]].
